articles.title: Rochdale Council Launches Preparing for Adulthood Strategy for Young People in Care
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council has introduced a new strategy aimed at assisting young people in care as they transition into adulthood, with a focus on education and personal development.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council has launched its new Preparing for Adulthood strategy, designed to support young people in care as they transition into adulthood. The initiative was unveiled at a special event held at Spotland Mills, where young people, councillors, members of Rochdale’s Parents Carers Voice, and council staff gathered to discuss the importance of this support.

The strategy aims to make the journey from childhood to adulthood easier and more positive for young people aged 14 to 25, along with their families and carers. The council's Preparing for Adulthood Team will assist young individuals in finding the appropriate support as they move from children's services into adult social care.

Before reaching the age of 18, the council will conduct an assessment to identify the care and support needs of each young person. For those deemed eligible, a new support plan will be developed to help them continue their education, acquire new skills, and access any additional support required by the young person or their family.

The event featured contributions from young people who highlighted the significance of feeling valued and supported during this critical transition into adulthood. This initiative reflects the council's commitment to ensuring that young people in care receive the necessary guidance and resources to thrive as they enter adulthood.

articles.title: Trams Cancelled Between Oldham and Rochdale for Two Weeks Due to Major Works
articles.excerpt: All tram services between Oldham and Rochdale will be suspended for nearly two weeks as part of significant Metrolink upgrades, with a replacement bus service available for affected passengers.
articles.content_html:
All tram services between Oldham and Rochdale will be suspended for nearly two weeks starting today, Monday, August 17, as part of ongoing major works on the Metrolink lines. The closure affects the entire stretch from Oldham Mumps to Rochdale Town Centre, with no trams running until Friday, August 28.

This closure follows a weekend of engineering works on the Rochdale line, which saw a complete halt of tram services from Rochdale Town Centre to Manchester Victoria. Stops affected by the current closure include Shaw, Newhey, and Milnrow, which are all part of the route between Oldham and Rochdale.

Passengers holding tram tickets will be able to use a replacement bus service during this period. The track renewal works are part of a £150 million upgrade to the Metrolink network, which is the largest in its history. Previous closures in July affected the Eccles, Trafford Centre, and Altrincham lines for three weeks as part of the same upgrade initiative.

Ian Davies, network director for Metrolink, expressed gratitude to passengers for their patience during the disruptions. He noted that Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has taken passenger feedback into account regarding the reliability of replacement bus services and is committed to improving the experience for commuters as the upgrade progresses.
